title: World population passes two billion
note: It took all of human history to reach the first billion and about 120 years to add the second. The pace of the next additions is the backdrop to every resource argument on this page.
limitations: UN estimate; year-only dating.

title: Oil is struck in Saudi Arabia
note: The seventh well at Dammam came in after six dry ones. Within a decade the kingdom's fields were the strategic fact of the Middle East.

title: The US president and the Saudi king meet on a warship
note: Security for oil, in a conversation on a cruiser in the Suez Canal on the way home from Yalta. The arrangement has outlasted every other from that week.

title: Iran nationalizes its oil industry
note: Parliament took the British-run fields, Britain blockaded the exports, and two years later a coup restored the concession. The memory of it runs under every negotiation with Tehran since.

title: World population passes three billion
note: One more billion in thirty-three years. The Green Revolution that fed it was still eight years away.
limitations: UN estimate; year-only dating.

title: Soviet planners divert the rivers that feed the Aral Sea
note: Cotton irrigation in the desert dried the fourth largest lake in the world to a tenth of its size within a lifetime. The five states that inherited the basin still argue over what is left.
limitations: Year-only dating; diversion expanded through the 1960s.

title: Five exporters found OPEC
note: Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Venezuela organized against the companies that set their prices. Thirteen years later they set the price themselves.

title: India and Pakistan divide the Indus rivers by treaty
note: Brokered by the World Bank, the treaty survived three wars and sixty-five years. It is the standard example of water cooperation between enemies.

title: India's wheat harvest jumps with new seed
note: High-yield varieties, fertilizer and irrigation took India from famine warnings to surplus in a decade. The relief it bought is the reason food stress fell off the war agenda for a generation.
limitations: Year-only dating.

title: US crude production peaks, as predicted
note: A geologist had forecast the year in 1956. Three years later the embargo showed what dependence on imports meant, and it shaped forty years of policy until shale reversed the curve.
limitations: Year-only dating.

title: The Soviet Union quietly buys up American grain
note: A crop failure sent Soviet buyers through American exporters before anyone noticed, and world prices tripled. Food became a Cold War lever in both directions.

title: Drought and famine across the Sahel
note: Six years of failed rains killed about 100,000 people and most of the region's livestock. The states that emerged from it are the ones now fighting insurgencies from Mali to Chad.
limitations: Year-only dating; the drought ran 1968 to 1974. Death toll estimates vary.

title: The first World Food Conference
note: After two years of price spikes and famine warnings, governments met in Rome and pledged that no child would go to bed hungry within a decade. The machinery it created still runs; the pledge did not.

title: China limits families to one child
note: A demographic brake applied by the state for thirty-five years. The working-age population it produced is now shrinking, which shapes how much time the leadership believes it has.

title: Mexico cannot pay, and the Latin American debt crisis begins
note: A weekend announcement that the country was out of reserves pulled a decade of petrodollar lending into default across the region. The lost decade that followed shaped the region's politics for thirty years.

title: Oil falls by two thirds
note: Saudi Arabia stopped defending the price and flooded the market. The Soviet Union, which sold oil for hard currency, lost the income it needed at the moment its reforms began.
limitations: Year-only dating; the fall ran through the first half of 1986.

title: Five billion people, and a day named for it
note: The UN marked the day in Zagreb. Twelve years per billion was the fastest the curve ever ran.

title: Six billion people
note: Marked in Sarajevo, four years after that city's siege ended. Growth was already slowing in most of the world and accelerating in the Sahel.

title: A European heat wave kills about 70,000 people
note: The deadliest weather event in modern European history, mostly older people in cities. It reset what governments expected a hot summer to cost.
limitations: Month-precision date; excess-death estimates range from 30,000 to 70,000.

title: Food prices double and riots follow in more than thirty countries
note: Oil at record highs, biofuel mandates, export bans and a weak dollar pushed rice and wheat to multiples of their 2006 prices. Governments fell in Haiti and wobbled elsewhere.
limitations: Month-precision date at the peak of the price run.

title: Oil touches 147 dollars a barrel
note: The peak of a five-year run driven by Chinese demand and flat supply, two months before the financial crisis cut it by three quarters.

title: Russia bans grain exports after drought and fires
note: The world's third largest wheat exporter shut its border and prices rose by half within months. The bread-price link to the uprisings that began in December is often cited and hard to prove.
limitations: The causal link to the Arab Spring is argued, not established.

title: China halts rare earth exports to Japan
note: After a boat collision near disputed islands, shipments of the metals Japan's industry ran on stopped for two months. Every later mineral policy in Tokyo, Washington and Brussels dates from this.
limitations: China denied an official embargo; the stoppage is documented in customs data.

title: A street vendor's protest starts the Arab Spring
note: One act of desperation in a provincial town became a wave that removed four governments and started two civil wars. Food prices, youth unemployment and a decade of frozen politics were the fuel.

title: The UN declares famine in Somalia
note: Drought, an insurgency that blocked aid, and a slow donor response killed about a quarter of a million people, half of them children. Famine in this century is a political event, not a weather one.

title: Seven billion people
note: The year of the Arab Spring, whose crowds were the largest youth cohort in the region's history entering a labor market that had no room for them.

title: The Islamic State declares a caliphate
note: A group that had taken Mosul three weeks earlier claimed a state across Syria and Iraq. It drew an international coalition, Russian intervention and Iranian militias into the same theater.

title: OPEC declines to cut, and oil halves
note: Saudi Arabia chose market share over price to squeeze American shale. Venezuela, Nigeria and Russia absorbed the loss; the cartel's grip on the price was shown to have limits.

title: Iran and six powers sign the nuclear deal
note: Enrichment capped and inspected in return for sanctions relief. For three years it was the most intrusive verification regime ever accepted by a state.

title: More than a million people cross into Europe in a year
note: War in Syria, collapse in Libya and stalled economies pushed the largest movement of people into Europe since 1945. The politics of half the continent turned on it within two years.
limitations: Month-precision date; the flow peaked in late summer and autumn.

title: Britain votes to leave the European Union
note: The first departure from the bloc, decided by a narrow majority. It weakened the union's weight in the security arguments that followed and consumed a decade of British politics.

title: A coup attempt fails in Turkey
note: Parts of the military moved on Ankara and Istanbul and lost within a night. The purge that followed reshaped NATO's second largest army.

title: About 700,000 Rohingya flee Myanmar into Bangladesh
note: A military clearance operation emptied northern Rakhine in weeks. The camps at Cox's Bazar are still the largest in the world.

title: North Korea tests a weapon it calls a hydrogen bomb
note: The sixth and largest test, about ten times the yield of the previous one, followed two intercontinental missile launches that summer. Deterrence in the Pacific changed shape in one year.

title: Venezuela's collapse sends millions abroad
note: Hyperinflation and a broken oil industry drove the largest displacement in the hemisphere's history, most of it into Colombia, Peru and Brazil. Migration became the lever of regional politics.
limitations: Year-only dating; the outflow ran from about 2015.

title: Cape Town counts down to Day Zero
note: A three-year drought took a city of four million to within weeks of shutting off its taps. Rationing and rain postponed the day; the map of which cities are next did not change.
limitations: Month-precision date; the countdown was announced in January 2018.

title: The United States becomes the world's largest crude producer
note: Shale took American output past Russia and Saudi Arabia. Energy independence changed what the country was willing to risk in the Gulf.
limitations: Year-only dating; the crossover was reported during 2018.

title: The United States leaves the Iran nuclear deal
note: Sanctions returned and Iran stepped away from its limits over the following year. Every strike on Iranian nuclear sites since has been argued from this decision.

title: The US and North Korean leaders meet for the first time
note: A page of promises and a pause in tests. The follow-up summit collapsed eight months later, and the tests resumed.

title: The United States and China begin tariffing each other
note: The first tranche covered 34 billion dollars each way and grew to cover most of the trade between the two largest economies. Interdependence, the argument for peace since 1990, started to run in reverse.
metricName: Goods covered by the first tariff round

title: A million people march in Hong Kong
note: Protests against an extradition law ran for months and ended with a national security law that closed the city's separate politics. Taiwan watched and drew its own conclusion.

title: The INF treaty ends
note: The 1987 ban on intermediate-range missiles lapsed after each side accused the other of cheating. The class of weapons that had been removed from Europe is being rebuilt on both sides.

title: Drones and missiles knock out half of Saudi oil output
note: The attack on Abqaiq and Khurais halted about 5.7 million barrels a day, the largest single supply disruption in history. Production was back within weeks; the lesson about air defense was not.
limitations: Attribution contested: Yemen's Houthis claimed it; the US and Saudi Arabia blamed Iran.

title: A US drone kills Iran's top general at Baghdad airport
note: Iran answered five days later with ballistic missiles on two bases housing American troops, the first direct state-on-state strike on US forces in decades. Both sides then stepped back.

title: The worst desert locust upsurge in decades reaches East Africa
note: Two unusual cyclone seasons bred swarms across the Arabian peninsula and the Horn. It arrived in the same weeks as the pandemic and competed with it for attention and money.
limitations: Month-precision date.

title: The WHO declares a pandemic
note: Borders closed, supply chains broke and governments spent at wartime scale. Trust between the major powers, already low, did not survive the argument over where it came from.
limitations: Reported deaths understate the toll; WHO excess-death estimates run to about 15 million by the end of 2021.
metricName: Reported deaths (excess-death estimates are several times higher)

title: A barrel of oil sells for less than nothing
note: With storage full and demand gone, the expiring US futures contract settled below zero. Petro-states lost a year of revenue in a quarter.

title: Ethiopia completes the first filling of its Nile dam
note: Egypt, which depends on the river for nearly all its water, called the unilateral filling an existential threat. Three fillings later there is still no agreement on how the dam is run in a drought.

title: A crowd storms the US Capitol to stop a transfer of power
note: The certification was delayed by hours, not stopped. Allies and rivals both re-priced the stability of the country that underwrites the alliance system.

title: Kabul falls and the twenty-year war ends
note: The government collapsed before the last American troops had left. The speed of it was read in Moscow and Beijing as a measure of American staying power six months before Ukraine.

title: The FAO food price index hits an all-time high
note: The invasion of Ukraine took a fifth of world wheat exports off the market in the same month, on top of energy and fertilizer costs already at records. Importers from Egypt to Lebanon felt it first.
limitations: Dated to the release week; the index is published monthly.

title: Monsoon floods put a third of Pakistan under water
note: About 33 million people were affected and a country already in a debt crisis lost a harvest. Climate loss and damage got its first line item at the UN talks that autumn.
limitations: Start date is when the monsoon flooding began; the worst came in August.

title: Sri Lanka's president flees as crowds take the palace
note: Months of fuel and food shortages after a sovereign default ended with protesters in the presidential pool. A debt crisis became a legitimacy crisis in one season.

title: Russia throttles gas to Europe
note: Deliveries through the main pipeline fell to a fifth of normal and then to zero. Europe spent hundreds of billions on substitutes and subsidies; gas as a weapon was tried and mostly absorbed.
limitations: Dated to the pipeline's maintenance shutdown; flows had been cut in steps since June.

title: The Black Sea Grain Initiative reopens Ukraine's ports
note: A UN and Turkish brokered deal let grain ships sail through a war zone. About 33 million tonnes moved in a year, and prices came off their peak within weeks of the signing.

title: Explosions destroy the Nord Stream pipelines
note: Three of four lines were breached on the Baltic seabed. Whoever did it, the option of turning the gas back on was gone.
limitations: Attribution unresolved in public sources.

title: Eight billion people
note: Eleven years for the last billion, and the UN expects the next to take fifteen. Growth is now concentrated in eight countries, most of them already under food and water stress.

title: Russia suspends the last arms control treaty
note: Inspections had already stopped; the announcement made it official. The treaty expired three years later with nothing to replace it.

title: India passes China as the most populous country
note: The UN's crossover estimate. One country is young and growing, the other is aging and shrinking, and both read the fact as a statement about the next fifty years.

title: Russia leaves the grain deal and strikes the ports
note: The corridor closed and the port of Odesa was bombed the same week. Food exports became a target again, which is what the deal had existed to prevent.

title: 2023 confirmed as the hottest year on record
note: About 1.48 degrees above the pre-industrial average, with every day of the year above one degree. The climate signal moved from projection to measurement.

title: Famine confirmed in a Darfur displacement camp
note: The first famine declaration anywhere since Somalia in 2011, in a camp of about half a million people besieged by one side of Sudan's war. Starvation was a tactic, not an accident.
limitations: Dated to the IPC review; the determination was published 1 August 2024.

title: 2024 is the first calendar year more than 1.5 degrees above pre-industrial
note: About 1.6 degrees, on the Copernicus record. One year is not the Paris threshold, which is a twenty-year average, but the line was crossed on the calendar.

title: The United States announces tariffs on nearly every trading partner
note: A baseline tariff on all imports and higher rates for dozens of countries, announced from the White House lawn. Markets fell for a week and China answered within days.

title: China restricts exports of seven rare earths
note: Announced two days after sweeping US tariffs, the licensing rules covered metals used in magnets, aircraft and missiles. Supply, not price, became the pressure point.

title: India holds the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance
note: The day after an attack in Kashmir, India suspended the treaty that had survived every previous war. Two weeks later the two countries were exchanging missiles.

title: Famine confirmed in Gaza governorate
note: The IPC confirmed famine in the north of the strip after twenty-two months of war and restricted aid. It was the first famine determination in the Middle East.
